data.argument: The constructive read is that growth is showing up across both development and water: revenue rose 60%, net income 31%, and EBITDA 29%, while water and wastewater revenue more than doubled, deliveries climbed to 631 acre-feet from 76, and taps sold increased to 66 from 40. Lot sales also grew 19%, supporting the Sky Ranch conversion thesis, and the company still expects Phase 2D substantially complete by fiscal year-end with Phase 2E paced to builder absorption. The model already contains the reported earnings and water-revenue figures, so this is confirmation rather than a quantified forecast beat. Cash fell to $8.44 million, and development-linked revenue plus untested timing and demand kill criteria counsel against extrapolating one strong quarter.
key_points: Water demand and tap sales accelerated year over year.
Lot sales rose; Phase 2D/2E plans remain constructive.
Cash declined, and no matching forecast allows a surprise calculation.
assumptions: Reported year-over-year comparisons are informative but do not establish sustained trends.
Company guidance is achievable; the supplied facts do not test prior timing against the two-quarter slip threshold.
